content: 1. Bitor may increase the systemic exposure (AUC) of unconjugated MMAE, potentially leading to enhanced toxicities associated with polatuzumab vedotin. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Atazanavir reduces the effects of pramlintide through mechanisms involving insulin resistance, as seen with protease inhibitors. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been documented. Use caution and monitor. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 4. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Atazanavir increases the levels of protriptyline through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Interrupt quizartinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors and resume the prior dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 12. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce rifabutin dose by up to 75% (e.g., 150 mg every other day or three times per week). Monitor for rifabutin-associated adverse reactions. 15. Atazanavir increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Start riociguat at 0.5 mg three times daily in patients receiving atazanavir. Monitor for signs and symptoms of hypotension during initiation and treatment. 17. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 18. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both atazanavir and ritonavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 19. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Atazanavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through mechanisms involving insulin resistance, as seen with protease inhibitors. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been documented. Use caution and monitor. 23. Atazanavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider alternatives if available due to increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 24. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 25. Atazanavir increases the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider alternatives due to the potential for increased toxicity and systemic effects. 26. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Limit saxagliptin to 2.5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Atazanavir increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Exercise caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Atazanavir increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor due to the potential for increased toxicity. 29. Atazanavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through mechanisms involving insulin resistance, as seen with protease inhibitors. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been documented. Use caution and monitor. 30. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 31. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, limit use to less than 14 days and monitor for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 34. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Stiripentol affects atazanavir levels by acting as both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. 36. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 37. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Atazanavir increases the levels of tadalafil by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Stop tadalafil more than 24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors, restart 7 days after initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 40. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 43. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Atazanavir increases the levels of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor due to the potential for increased toxicity. 45. Atazanavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Ritonavir boosting may help compensate for this interaction. 46. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 48. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Atazanavir increases the levels of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 51. Atazanavir enhances the effects of timolol through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor. Increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 52. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both atazanavir and tipranavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 54. Atazanavir increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to MMAE, raising the risk of adverse effects. 55. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Atazanavir increases the levels of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Toremifene metabolism may be inhibited by drugs that inhibit CYP3A4. 57. Atazanavir increases the levels of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor due to the potential for increased toxicity. 58. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 59. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 60. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Atazanavir increases the levels of trimipramine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 63. Ublituximab decreases the effects of atazanavir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 64. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate; co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 66. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Exercise caution if upadacitinib is co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 67. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 68. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if weight >50 kg. 69. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Limit vardenafil to 5 mg/24 hr. 70. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 71. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Increased risk of AV block. 72. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates; co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 73. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of warfarin through mechanisms involving the metabolism of its less potent R-enantiomer by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor.
